card.name: Frequency and degree words after clauses
card.fires_on: Quantity or frequency words such as more, the, every, many, most, any, that, right after a clause or a 'times' phrase. They begin an adverbial of comparison or frequency, like 'more often than' or 'the same'.

modes.label: Comparative 'more' after times
modes.description: The word 'more' follows 'times' or a clause and leads into 'often than' or 'than men'.
modes.example: Women are diagnosed with CFS two to four times<< more>> often than men, according to researchers.

modes.label: Other frequency or degree adverbials
modes.description: Words like the, every, many, most, any, that begin phrases such as 'the same', 'every time', 'many times', 'most of the time', 'any more than'.
modes.example: Beowulf has been translated into Modern English<< many>> times.

card.writes: It seems to push away from ordinary continuations and toward unusual word pieces, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It marks the small word that starts a phrase of how often or how much, like 'more often than' or 'every time'.
